verse: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.
reflect: Advent begins in the dark on purpose. Isaiah spoke to people who could not see a way forward, and promised light before they could see it. Hope is not pretending the dark isn't there; it is trusting the light that is coming.
ask: Where do you need a little light this week?
cta: Read Isaiah 9 chapter by chapter, with plain-English context, in Wayfold

verse: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
reflect: The busiest month of the year is the one named for the Prince of Peace. Peace here is not a quiet calendar; it is Someone carrying the weight we can't. This week, hand one worry back to him.
ask: What is one thing you could stop carrying this week?
cta: Find a verse for the real-life moment you're in, every day, in Lampstep

verse: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
reflect: The first people to hear the news were shepherds on the night shift. Joy came to ordinary people doing ordinary work. Joy is one of the fruits of the Spirit, and it grows in small, daily places.
ask: Who could you bring a little joy to this week?
cta: Grow one fruit of the Spirit at a time, with small daily practices, in Ninefruit

verse: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
reflect: Christmas is a gift before it is a holiday. Love gave first, and gave the best. As the week fills with gifts and gatherings, let each one point back to the first one.
ask: Christmas trivia for the car ride: how many wise men does the Bible say came? (Answer: it doesn't say. It names three gifts.)
cta: Play Bible trivia and story games together as a family in Scrollway

verse: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
reflect: Welcome, whether this is your first Christmas service or your fiftieth. The heart of the story is short enough to fit on this card: God came close. Read Luke 2 tonight before you go to bed.
ask: What part of the Christmas story do you want to understand better?
cta: Understand the Bible one chapter at a time, starting with Luke 2, in Wayfold

verse: It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
reflect: New year's resolutions fade by February. God's mercies don't: they are new every morning, including the morning after you slip. Start small and start daily.
ask: Men: what is one daily habit you want to keep through 2027?
cta: Men: start a 90-day daily Bible plan built for real life in FORGED

theme: A lamp for the next step
verse: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
reflect: A lamp doesn't light the whole road, just the next step. You don't need the whole year figured out; you need light for today's decision.
ask: What decision do you need light for this week?
cta: Get a verse for the moment you're in, at work, at home or in conflict, in Lampstep

verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
reflect: Fruit isn't made in a day; it grows. Paul lists nine fruits, and none of them is forced. Pick one this week and practise it at home, at school or at work.
ask: Kids: which fruit will you practise this week, and how?
cta: Families: grow the fruit of the Spirit together, one small practice a day, in Ninefruit
